source_reports.citation: Wagner, D.M., Krieger, J.D., and Veilleux, A.G., 2016, Methods for estimating annual exceedance probability discharges for streams in Arkansas, based on data through water year 2013: U.S. Geological Survey Scientific Investigations Report 2016-5081, 136 p.
Anderson, B.T., 2021, Magnitude and frequency of floods in the alluvial plain of the lower Mississippi River, 2017: U.S. Geological Survey Scientific Investigations Report 2021-5046, 15 p.

notes: Wagner and others, SIR 2016-5081 (no later version on the publication page): flood regions A, B1, B2, C and D at 7 AEPs (no 0.5 percent), and Anderson, SIR 2021-5046: the Mississippi Alluvial Plain (MAP) at 8 AEPs. Equations as printed: Table 7's 10**(... -0.297(0.01*LC11PAST+1) ...) terms are identity variables with scale 0.01 and offset 1, so Table 11's U stays in its printed basis; NSS folds them into its intercept and coefficients, which is the same equation. Ranges from Table 10, MEV and U (order as headed) from Table 11, AVP and Sp from Table 7. Region B1 and B2 carry the report's 500 ft ELEV gate. Both current: region D and MAP are co-located in eastern Arkansas (NSS locates both at 07077500 and 07077950), and they are kept as separate regions with no preference. SIR 2021-5046 says it updates the MAP and calls 2016-5081 a recent publication for a subsection, but nowhere says it supersedes region D, and NSS has D at status 4 (enabled for StreamStats) and GC1917 at status 3 (enabled for NSS, disabled for StreamStats). Table 11 misprints, settled because only the corrected values make the matrix positive definite and reproduce Table 7's AVP from MEV + mean xUx at the region's 56 gages: B2 Q50% intercept-SOILINDEX prints -0.010697946 in both cells (mean 0.618 against AVP 0.025), stored as -0.10697946 (0.0249), a decimal-shift correction printed nowhere; B2 Q1% ALVM-intercept prints -0.01477342 against -0.011477342 in the intercept row, stored as the latter; B2 Q0.2% SOILINDEX-intercept prints -0.017874274 against -0.1787427 in the intercept row, stored as the latter. Table 7 B1 Q0.2% prints Sp 46.86 percent, which does not match its own AVP 0.042 (49.9 percent) and MEV + mean xUx gives 0.0420: kept as printed in sep_log, and intervals use the covariance there anyway. Every other AVP closes. NSS differs: its SEP at all 35 region A-D equations is Table 7's 'Values from Hodge and Tasker (1995)' column, not this report's Sp; its ranges round BSHAPE, ELEV, PRECIP, LC11PAST, SLPFM (A ELEV max 1,840 for 1,832.27). Table 10 differs slightly from the Table 8 gages: B1 minimum area 0.10 (a 0.06 gage), B2 minimum ELEV 168.88 (168.52), B2 maximum area 2,090 (2,092), D maximum area 1,620 (1,622); and the 500 ft gate has a gage on the wrong side in each subregion (493.94 ft in B1, 500.55 ft in B2). Table 10 is stored. No worked example in either report. Per-gage: all 281 Table 9 RRE flows at Table 8's characteristics, and the 50 gages Table 3 of SIR 2021-5046 prints (its title says 58, 8 of Table 1's gages have no row). Not stored, no schema field: Table 7 MSE (of unweighted residuals, distinct from MEV), pseudo-R2, SEM; Table 11's t (reproduced from n_sites); Table 12's area-ratio exponents; SIR 2021-5046's MSE column (0.034 to 0.061), which is not stored as a model error variance because it exceeds AVP at 5 AEPs and the report prints no matrix, so MAP intervals use AVP. SIR 2021-5046 limits: not applicable where more than 10 percent of the basin is impervious, nor under substantial regulation (text, not stored). Variable codes are NSS's: SLPFM is CSLBlue, BSHAPE is BSHAPELFP, and NSS gives MAP's slope in Arkansas as CSL1085LFP, though the slope in Table 1 equals region D's SLPFM at shared gages and is close to live CSLBlue, not CSL1085LFP (07077950: 0.81 printed, CSLBlue 0.82, CSL1085LFP 0.71, which lowers its Q1% from the printed 8,430 to 7,939).
